the model declares the slot indices as named constants rather than as inline literals. mechanics.body_shape: two register saves; the receiver aliased out of ECX and the source read from the stack; a pointer-identity guard that refuses the whole operation on a self-reference; a conditional detach-and-release of the word the receiver holds at displacement 0x30; then two unconditional dispatches on the receiver, the second through a fresh read of the receiver's table pointer, the last of the three given the source as its single stack word; a shared epilogue and a callee-cleaned return.
mechanics.guard: if (receiver == other) return; -- 0x006a14d8 CMP ESI,EDI with 0x006a14da JZ 0x006a1504. Pointer identity only: no alias test, no offset test and no range test appears anywhere in the 25 instructions. A self-reference dispatches nothing at all -- no detach, no release, no clear, no add -- and the branch target is the epilogue, so nothing has to be undone on the way out.

receiver_displacement.0x30: read at 0x006a14dc (MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x30]) and written at 0x006a14e3 (MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x30],0x0). This is the body's only read through a receiver displacement other than zero and its only write. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates exactly two displacements, 0x0 and 0x30, with bounds_only true, and names no member for either.

mechanics.held_word_read: 0x006a14dc loads the word into ECX. Nothing between that load and 0x006a14ef overwrites ECX, and the store at 0x006a14e3 goes through ESI rather than through ECX, so the register still holds the loaded word. That is what makes the following transfer a call ON the held object rather than on the receiver.
mechanics.held_word_null_test: 0x006a14df TEST ECX,ECX with 0x006a14e1 JZ 0x006a14f1. The target 0x006a14f1 is the receiver's own first dispatch and not the store, so a null word skips the store AND the transfer together and leaves the receiver's word exactly as it was found.
mechanics.detach: receiver+0x30 = 0, executed BEFORE the transfer at 0x006a14ef. The ordering is observable and is preserved in the source: anything reached through that transfer sees the word already cleared. Why the order is this way is not established by any record for this target -- 0x00432b50's own listing shows no path that reads a child's word at 0x30 -- so the order is modelled and the motivation is left unclaimed.

Whether the detached word is owned, borrowed or a counted handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed here.

unresolved_questions: What is the word the receiver holds at displacement 0x30? The machine supports exactly three claims: it is 4 bytes wide, it is compared against zero and it is dispatched through slot +0x04 of a table reached by dereferencing it. Whether it is a parent, an owner, a back-link or something else is not established by any record for this target, and the name mpParent is decompiler-derived from the imported SDK symbols. The model types it only as an object whose first word is a table pointer, which is the least that survives the evidence.

Why is the word detached before it is released? The store at 0x006a14e3 precedes the transfer at 0x006a14ef and the order is observable. Nothing in this body states a reason, and 0x00432b50's own listing shows no path that reads a child's word at 0x30, so the motivation is not recoverable from what is here. It reads like an unlink-then-release to break a cycle or to satisfy a re-entrancy invariant in the callee; that is a reading, not a record, and is not modelled as one.

Is 0x00432b50 the right slot +0x04 target at run time? Both table images agree on it, which is as strong as static evidence gets, but the transfer is dispatched on the HELD OBJECT and that object's dynamic type may be a third class not represented by either image.

Why is slot +0x48 overridden but slot +0x38 not? The two images share this body at +0x34 and the same 0x006a1510 at +0x38, yet carry different targets at +0x48. Whether the source-adding step was deliberately left un-overridden because it must behave identically for both list kinds, or was simply never needed as an override, is not decidable from the images alone.

Can the re-read of the receiver's table pointer at 0x006a14fa matter? The listing reads it twice, and this body models the re-read. Whether anything between the two reads can change the receiver's table pointer is not determinable from this body, and neither of the two +0x48 targets has been characterised for such a write here.

Can the adding step see a stale view of the source? 0x006a1510 reads its argument's word at displacement 0x30 and, when it is non-null, recurses through its own slot +0x38 before calling its own slot +0x30. This body has just cleared the RECEIVER, and on every path past the guard the source is a different object, so the interaction is presumably benign -- but this body performs no check that would make it so, and the recursion inside 0x006a1510 is not characterised here.

Who calls this, and with what? fan_in is 0, callers is empty and the only two xrefs are the table placements. Nothing establishes the entry conditions, so no precondition, no aliasing expectation beyond the pointer-identity guard, and no null-source expectation is claimed.

Which of the two table images is the receiver at run time? The body is shared and the +0x48 step is the only one that differs, so the answer changes which clearing code runs. Nothing in the evidence picks one, and the model dispatches through the table pointer in memory, which is the honest shape rather than a choice.

tooling_findings: RETURN SEMANTICS cannot pass for this target, and the cause is a category mismatch in the validator. _abi_category (tools/reconstruction_tooling/validate.py) reads categories['abi'] and never categories['abi_derived'], so when a pack keeps the machine ABI in a separate abi_derived envelope -- which this one does -- the derived return classification never reaches the check. This target's categories.abi_derived.value carries schema 'openspore-abi-inference-1' and, inside it, abi.return_semantics = 'unclassified_in_EAX' and abi.return = {register: EAX, type: null, void_possible: false}; _abi_category returns the PERSISTED abi instead, which has neither return_type nor return_semantics, so _abi_claim yields None. By contrast _machine_record does consult abi_derived first, which is why the receiver, parse and dispatch records resolve fine and CONSTANTS, FIELDS/OFFSETS and VIRTUAL DISPATCH all have their machine side. Reported, not fixed.

The consequence for a void target is that the check is unreachable in the passing direction: even a source declaring the record's own token gets NOT_AVAILABLE. cases.honest_accounting: This is a real gap in the test, not a gap in the reconstruction, and it is not closable through this interface. The store's guard is 'the word is non-null', so the only state in which the mutation differs is one where the word is already null and the value written is null: a byte-for-byte no-op. Distinguishing them needs the number of memory writes rather than their result, i.e. a hardware watchpoint, and the test observes bytes. The limitation is stated in a comment on the test that checks the receiver is not written. The reconstruction is correct here: the listing does put the store inside the TEST/JZ, and the model puts it inside the if.

mutation_check.verdict: The test has teeth. Nine distinct machine-level mistakes are each caught by at least one named assertion, and the one survivor is a documented observability limit rather than a hole in the reconstruction. A reader who wants a stricter test would need write-counting instrumentation, which is outside what a plain model test can see.
